speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are a 3-week history of fatigue, easy bruising, fever, and severe leg pain. These symptoms are concerning for a bone marrow issue. To start my evaluation, are you a child or an infant, and have you noticed any bone swelling or difficulty walking with the leg pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing generalized fatigue and easy bruising for 3 weeks. Over the past week, she has developed a fever and severe leg pain that wakes her up at night.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the combination of night pain, fever, bruising, and fatigue is highly concerning for acute leukemia. Given her age, I need to assess her current stability. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count with differential. REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray of the affected leg.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, Leukocyte_Count 63,000/mm3 (elevated), Platelet_Count 27,000/mm3 (decreased); Bone_Marrow_Aspirate: Findings predominantly immature cells that are positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL). The clinical presentation of fatigue, bruising, and bone pain, combined with CBC showing anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukocytosis, along with the bone marrow aspirate revealing immature lymphoid blasts (CD10+, CD19+, TdT+), confirms this diagnosis.
